distractors.reason: We don't say 'text letter'. A letter is a paper message sent by post, not a message sent on a phone.
We don't say 'text note'. A note is a short handwritten piece of paper, not a phone message.
We don't say 'text call'. A call is spoken on the phone, while a text is written.

example_sentence: Please send me a text ___ when you arrive.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku mogą odwrócić kolejność słów i powiedzieć 'message text' zamiast 'text message', ponieważ w języku polskim najpierw stoi rzeczownik główny ('wiadomość'), a przymiotnik po nim.
explanation: In English, the first noun in a noun-noun compound describes the second one: a 'text message' is a message sent as text. Learners should keep the modifier before the head noun.

related_collocations.example: I had a phone call from the bank this morning.
He left me a voice message while I was at work.
We were stuck in a traffic jam for an hour.

memory_tip: TEXT + MESSAGE = a written message sent by phone | MESSAGE is the head noun, TEXT describes it
